question: Do neighbouring gold windows share a verdict, and is the start of a clip irrelevant?
data: IndEgo human gold, 150 windows / 7 clips (human labels)
method: Nearest-neighbour label agreement; bad rate by position
headline_result: Neighbour agreement 0.73 vs 0.56 chance (n=143 pairs, ~15 s apart); first-120 s bad rate 0.19 vs 0.42 later.
why: Sparse sampling is plausible, but 'skip the start' is NOT supported on IndEgo (the start is the cleaner part). Test change-point-driven sampling, not a fixed skip rule.

question: How few frames/s keep the pixel-feature accuracy?
data: IndEgo gold 150 windows (100 good / 50 bad, human)
method: Decode once at native 10 fps, deterministic index subsample, cpu_window_features with true fps, LOCO logistic C=0.3 + clip-bootstrap CI
why: 3.33 fps stays within 0.02 of full rate using 34 instead of 100 frames; 2 fps is borderline (-0.022). 3.33 fps adopted for the pixel view pending the OOD/EG2 combination.

question: Does the EG2 window embedding need fewer (or more) frames?
data: IndEgo gold 150 windows (human)
method: Cached segments.npz subsample + GPU-lock re-embed for 5/10 fps, LOCO logistic C=0.01
headline_result: LOCO n=150: 2 fps 0.848 [0.73,0.91], 1 fps 0.860, 0.5 fps 0.870 (CIs overlap; fewer frames NOT worse); two-view prob-avg 0.852-0.854.
why: EG2 needs no denser sampling; 5/10 fps re-embed only if GPU time remains. Deferred as 'maybe' because it does not change the frozen 2 fps view.

question: Does the frozen IndEgo model transfer to 1080p30 Egocentric-10K at any fps?
data: OOD labels n=60 (51 good / 9 bad, human; n_bad=9 EXPLORATORY)
method: Decode the original source at each fps, same features, frozen-model AUROC + rank stability + per-feature AUROC
headline_result: Frozen IndEgo logistic AUROC 0.36 [0.18,0.55] at 30 fps up to 0.55 at 2-3 fps - every CI95 includes 0.5. Score rank stability (Spearman) >= 0.98 for 5-vs-1 fps. Spatial features fps-invariant; band/rPPG features collapse.
why: Do NOT choose the OOD fps from an IndEgo-trained model. The OOD cost lever is DECODE (~3004 ms/window), not fps.

question: At an equal 20-frame budget, does any frame-selection strategy beat uniform?
data: IndEgo gold 150 windows (human)
method: 20-frame budget: uniform vs motion-adaptive vs keyframe-only vs seeded random, same LOCO protocol
headline_result: Uniform-20 0.787 [0.650,0.866]; motion-adaptive 0.762; keyframe-only 0.780; random 0.739 - all CI95 overlap; no arm beats uniform.
why: Keep uniform sampling (arange(0,T,5)); no arm reduces cost (the full window is decoded in every arm).

question: What are the clean per-stage costs (decode/features) on this pod, per regime?
data: n=1 IndEgo window + 1 Egocentric-10K 1080p window (no labels)
method: Cost re-bench: 3 reps x 3 bench runs, min-of-9, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, cv2 threads=1
headline_result: Clean minima: in-domain 480p decode 112 ms/window + features 289/167/102/54/32 ms at 10/5/3.33/2/1 fps; OOD 1080p HEVC decode 2900 ms/window. Shard-run means are 2.24-8.01x these clean minima.
why: Cite pareto.json for every clean cost number; do not quote a hand-typed shard/clean multiplier.

question: Can ONE tiled timestamped image replace N sequential frame evaluations at <=1/4 cost?
data: IndEgo gold 150 windows (human) + OOD 60 (51 good / 9 bad, human)
method: EmbeddingGemma-2 image embedding of a mosaic, logistic C=0.01 LOCO, clip-bootstrap CI; N in {4,6,9,12,16}, tile 224
headline_result: Mosaic 0.757-0.842 over N=4..100, below matched mean-of-frames 0.822-0.860 at almost every N; OOD 0.155-0.638 (often worse than chance).
why: Not within 0.02 AUROC of mean-of-frames on BOTH regimes; the one in-domain-near point (N=30) collapses OOD. Keep only as a human-evidence artefact.

question: What is the matched mean-of-frames accuracy the mosaic must beat?
data: Same windows/folds as E2.01 (human)
method: Mean of per-frame EmbeddingGemma-2 embeddings (same decoded frames), logistic LOCO
headline_result: Mean-of-frames 0.822-0.860 over N=4..100, reproducing the cached EG2 reference 0.848.
why: This is the control that stays the model input; it is the baseline the mosaic failed to match.

question: Does temporal/spatial tile layout carry signal beyond a bag of tiles?
data: Same windows/folds (human)
method: N=9 tile 224 with deterministic placement permutation (seed 1), same eval
headline_result: Shuffled 0.801 [0.64,0.89] vs ordered 0.785 [0.64,0.86]: difference inside CI; order is not load-bearing.
why: Layout is not load-bearing; the mosaic adds no information over pooled tiles.

question: Do burned-in timestamps add signal beyond the pixels?
data: Same windows/folds (human)
method: N=9 tile 224 with timestamps=False, same eval
headline_result: No-timestamp 0.810 [0.68,0.88] vs with-timestamps 0.785 [0.64,0.86]: +0.025 inside CI.
why: Timestamps are not load-bearing (weaker than the shuffled-tile control difference).

question: Lower bound: does one middle frame match an N-tile mosaic?
data: Same windows/folds (human)
method: 1x1 mosaic of the middle frame (t=5 s), same eval
headline_result: Single middle frame 0.784 [0.69,0.85] ~= mosaic N9 0.785 [0.64,0.86] at 1/N the embedding passes.
why: Tiling N frames adds nothing over a single frame in-domain; not adopted as a model input, but shows the mosaic's cost advantage is the only benefit.

question: Does a motion-energy mosaic carry the usable-window cue?
data: Same windows/folds (human)
method: N=9 tiles of abs consecutive-frame difference |I_t - I_{t-1}|, same eval
headline_result: Motion mosaic 0.863 [0.78,0.91] is the best in-domain variant, but OOD 0.401 (fails transfer).
why: Best in-domain but the motion cue is inverted/often head stability, not hand work; not adopted.

question: Does tiling layout/timestamps help beyond pooled per-tile statistics?
data: Same windows/folds (human)
method: concat(mean,std) of N=9 per-tile EmbeddingGemma-2 embeddings, same eval
headline_result: Pooled per-tile stats 0.826 [0.69,0.88] vs mosaic N9 0.785: layout is not load-bearing.
why: Confirms the no-layout control; the mosaic's structure adds no accuracy.

question: How much window sparsity keeps the clip-level verdict?
data: IndEgo gold 150 windows / 7 clips (human) + EG2/26-feat LOCO OOF probs
method: Per-clip subsampling simulation on gold-window order; label-oracle + OOF-score estimates; clip bad-fraction MAE, accept/reject @30%
headline_result: every-2: clip-frac error 0.049 [0.019,0.087], 7/7 verdicts @30%, delay 0.3 windows at 51% cost; every-3/4: 0.117/0.124; skip-first-M 0.088->0.418; CUSUM-default never fires.
why: Adopt every-2nd-window grid for IndEgo-like data; drop CUSUM-as-sampler and skip-first-M; random rejected on latency (delay 8.9 windows).

question: Does position in a 20-min Egocentric-10K clip predict bad windows?
data: OOD labels n=60 (51 good / 9 bad, human) + queue source_start_s + manifest durations
method: Logistic bad~position (raw + normalised) and Mann-Whitney bad vs good positions
headline_result: No position effect on OOD: MW p=0.42 raw / 0.47 normalised (n=60, n_bad=9); medians 70 s vs 90 s.
why: Skip-the-start is NOT justified for Egocentric-10K either (but n_bad=9 is thin); re-run at n_bad~24.

question: Does observing less than a 10 s window still separate good/bad?
data: IndEgo gold 150 windows (human); EG2 21-frame/2 fps embeddings
method: LOCO logistic on L2-normalised mean of the first 4/8/12/16/21 frames; AUROC vs seconds
why: Adopt observe-first-4-s early exit (IndEgo); never below 4 s. 2.5x window-cost cut; the OOD curve needs a working OOD scorer.

question: How many footage-hours per wall-hour do the sampling policies buy?
data: Egocentric-10K manifest 1546 windows / 4.404 h (unlabelled) + policy fractions from E3.01/E3.03
method: Arithmetic: fraction-windows-processed x within-window-seconds-fraction -> processed hours per footage hour
headline_result: 4.404 h corpus: every-2 -> 2.27 h (x1.9); every-2 + 4 s exit -> ~0.9 h (x4.9); every-3 + 4 s -> x7.2 (decode-bound upper bound).
why: Feed x4.9 adopted / x7.2 budget numbers to the E7 cost dashboard.

question: What is the single adopted sampling policy per data regime?
data: Synthesis of E3.01-E3.04 results JSONs
method: Tolerance-based selection on clip-level error; per-regime statement; evidence-thinness audit
headline_result: Adopt IndEgo: every-2nd + 4 s exit (~0.20 footage, x5). OOD: no certified policy (transfer fails; n_bad=9). Sampling is not the bottleneck (model error 0.167 at full coverage).
why: Freeze the E3 policy; unblock OOD on the E5 scorer; re-test position at n_bad~24. Passing tolerance was chosen post hoc on the same 7 clips (marginal).

question: Which deterministic descriptors separate IndEgo from Egocentric-10K beyond container spec?
data: 730 descriptor records: 150 IndEgo gold + 120 OOD-60 (480p/30 tc + 1080p/30 src) + 100 OOD-2 + 300 seed-7 Ego10K + 60 IndEgo-spec re-encodes
method: Deterministic per-window descriptors (ffprobe + 8 sampled-frame stats, no GPU); Cohen's d ranking
headline_result: Container separators are exact by construction; strongest CONTENT separators IndEgo-vs-OOD-source are chroma_spread d=-3.19, bright_frac -2.65, luma_mean -2.57, temp_energy -2.37; sharpness only d=0.61.
why: Use content separators to justify per-regime profiles; do not treat resolution/fps as findings.

question: Do blurry/low-light/walking terciles deserve their own models or thresholds?
data: 150 IndEgo gold windows (human), LOCO over 7 clips
method: Logistic (C=0.01, balanced) on 26 per-pixel feats and EG2 embedding; global vs regime-only; 2000x clip-bootstrap CI
headline_result: No regime split adopted; best feat26 cell lighting_lo +0.125 [-0.10,0.35]; EG2 regime models worse (-0.01..-0.18). Global feat26 0.712 [0.634,0.811], EG2 0.848 [0.719,0.912].
why: Keep one global model per view; regime-only never beat global by >0.03 with a supporting CI; motion terciles are thin (motion_lo n_bad=4).

question: Does re-encoding OOD to the IndEgo container spec fix transfer?
data: 60 OOD queue-1 windows (human, 9 bad); paired 1080p/30 source vs 480p/30 transcode vs 480x480/10 re-encode
method: ffmpeg re-encode; paired descriptors; IndEgo-vs-OOD Cohen's d before/after; frozen-ensemble score audit
headline_result: Re-encoding shrinks the content gap for only 6/18 descriptors; several grow (luma_p05 d -1.34 -> +5.02). Frozen-ensemble OOD AUROC 0.415 (n=60, n_bad=9) not improved.
why: Matching the container does not fix the content gap; keep container/spec as a router input only.

question: Can a deterministic router select the right pipeline per data type?
data: Synthetic descriptors + E4.01 descriptor ranges (n=730)
method: profiles/schema.json + 5 profiles + jadal/regimes/router.py::choose_profile; 13 unit tests (<30 s, no video)
headline_result: Deterministic router + 5 profiles + schema; 13/13 unit tests pass; UNSEEN_REGIME fallback range-checks decision descriptors; receipt_fragment() returns a helper dict (not yet wired into the receipt builder).
why: Ship the router + profiles so the product adapts to the received regime; wire receipt_fragment into the receipt builder in a later change.

question: Does the frozen ensemble reproduce its OOD prior on the 60 human windows?
data: 60 human OOD windows (51 good / 9 bad); frozen scores
method: Recompute frozen ensemble_v1 usable_prob AUROC vs the 60 labels; window bootstrap
headline_result: 0.415 AUROC [0.201,0.656] (window bootstrap, optimistic); balacc@0.5 0.471.
why: Reproduces the previously cited 0.415 headline; cited prior for the E5 report, not a new result.

question: Do EG2 frame heads trained on 10k AI-labelled factory frames carry window signal on IndEgo?
data: 10k AI-labelled FACTORY frames (AI, NOT human) + 150 IndEgo human gold windows
method: EG2 frame embeddings -> logistic heads (5-fold CV, C=1) -> pool per window -> LOCO over 7 clips + clip-bootstrap CI
headline_result: Pooled AI-frame heads on 150 IndEgo windows: work-prob mean 0.813 [0.695,0.864]; hands 0.818; both 0.826 [0.717,0.881]; 12-feat 0.789. Below the 0.85 in-domain EG2 baseline.
why: Keep pooled AI-frame heads as a cheap prior only; model-vs-model (AI head labels), NOT accuracy; do not claim transfer.

question: How many human OOD labels are needed to recover usable signal?
data: 60 Egocentric-10K human-labelled windows (51 good / 9 bad, 47 factories) + frozen EG2/pixel caches
method: Factory-grouped / leave-one-factory-out CV (StratifiedGroupKFold); logistic on pixel-26, EG2 means, two-view average
why: A ~12-window OOD adaptation set can recover ~0.7 AUROC on THIS set (exploratory); needs the 100-window batch + labels2 before any rate is quoted; smallest n_bad in a fold = 7.

question: Which of the 26 per-pixel features keep their sign from IndEgo to Egocentric-10K?
data: 150 IndEgo human gold windows + 60 OOD human-labelled windows (51 good / 9 bad)
method: Signed AUROC per feature; clip-bootstrap CI (IndEgo) and window-bootstrap CI (OOD, optimistic); stable/flip/chance
headline_result: 8 sign-stable (radial_slope 0.633/0.645, hf_ratio 0.618/0.693, dct_energy 0.631/0.702, luma_p05, global_shift, illum_r, illum_b, zncc_self); 14 flip (motion_energy 0.308->0.721, temp_b0 0.534->0.240, skin_frac 0.667->0.257); 4 chance.
why: Use the stable sharpness/light features for regime routing; do not reuse motion/temporal-band signs across domains.

question: Does the frozen ensemble transfer to the 160-window OOD batch?
data: 160 Egocentric-10K windows scored by frozen ensemble_v1; ood_labels2.json MISSING (n human labels = 0)
method: Load frozen scores; when ood_labels2.json appears, merge + window-bootstrap AUROC; until then descriptive distributions only
headline_result: labels2 NOT delivered: result records labels_missing=true, n=0, ci95=n/a. Descriptive: usable_prob mean 0.560; accept 71 / review 35 / reject 54. No accuracy computed.
why: Watcher eval/exp_domain/watch_e5_04.sh re-scores and runs the confirmatory eval automatically when ood_labels2.json appears.

question: Is the residual-motion cue just 'the wearer is not walking'?
data: IndEgo human gold 150 windows / 7 clips; cue recomputed, ego-motion from series_gold shift_px
method: Per-window mean residual motion after translation-only compensation at 160x90; within-tercile AUROC + Spearman partial correlation; clip-bootstrap CI
headline_result: Strongest motion scalar is ego-motion magnitude (shift_px mean), oriented AUROC 0.805 [0.675,0.893]. Residual cue oriented 0.692; partial correlation controlling for ego-motion -0.102 [-0.347,+0.072] (CI includes 0). Low-motion tercile is 49 good/1 bad.
why: Do not use the residual-motion cue as an independent signal; it is largely 'the wearer is not walking'. Keep ego-motion magnitude as a regime/stability descriptor.

question: Can a label-free per-clip sign calibration repair the inverted clips?
data: IndEgo human gold 150 windows / 7 clips (scoring); calibration uses only each clip's own unlabelled cue values
method: LOCO direction (6 train clips); per-clip label-free recalibration on the held-out clip (majority-prior sign; within-clip -|z|); pooled AUROC + clip-bootstrap CI
headline_result: Raw pooled 0.692 [0.477,0.839]; within-clip -|z| 0.606; majority-prior sign 0.610. Pallet 0.36->0.64 and organise 0.31->0.69 repaired but desk 0.73->0.27 broken. Oracle per-clip sign (upper bound) 0.757.
why: The pallet inversion cannot be fixed at inference without labels; the label-free rule trades one broken clip for two repaired and lowers pooled AUROC. No per-clip sign calibration.

question: Does the IndEgo-frozen motion-cue direction transfer to Egocentric-10K?
data: 60 human-labelled Egocentric-10K windows (51 good / 9 bad; EXPLORATORY)
method: Same cue extraction (160x90, translation-only); direction frozen from IndEgo; pooled AUROC + window-bootstrap CI (optimistic)
headline_result: IndEgo-frozen direction resid_mean AUROC 0.281 [0.145,0.434] - worse than chance; Spearman cue vs label +0.271, opposite sign to in-domain (-0.314). Post-hoc best orientation 0.719 (not usable).
why: Do not apply the IndEgo motion-cue direction out of domain; per-source sign calibration is not applicable (one labelled window per source).

question: Is the E6.01 conclusion robust to the stratification rule and logistic controls?
data: IndEgo human gold 150 windows / 7 clips; same cue/ego vectors as E6.01
method: 4 stratification rules (terciles, quintiles, fixed 5/15 px, fixed 1/5/20 px) x 4 cue variants; LOCO logistic cue-only vs ego-only vs cue+ego
headline_result: Interpretable strata span 0.503-0.756; LOCO logistic cue-only 0.660, ego-motion-only 0.798, cue+ego 0.793 (cue adds -0.005).
why: Negative result logged: the within-motion-level effect is weak and stratum-dependent; the cue adds nothing over ego-motion magnitude.

question: How many hours of video per wall-hour does the pod A40 deliver, per profile?
data: n/a (cost model): timings on the pod A40 + source JSONs E1.01, E1.02, E1.04, E2.01, E3.04; profiles/*.json
method: Timed decode (CPU ffmpeg vs NVDEC cuvid), pixel26 CPU features, EmbeddingGemma-2 batch-1 image embeddings on real mosaic PNGs; arithmetic cost model per profile
headline_result: Per-profile 0.51-15.22 video-h/wall-h; every-2nd+4s-exit pixel26 565 ms/window -> 35.4 vs 9.1 full sampling (x3.88 wall-clock; mosaic-only x4.14); embedding-bound at batch 1 (183 ms/image).
why: Use as the pod cost reference; keep NVDEC(1080p HEVC)/CPU(480p) separate; re-time on an idle pod. Policy verdicts stay with E3 (no new accuracy here; 3.88x < the 4x cost-only bar).

question: Can the frozen two-view recipe + profile router produce one deterministic contract JSONL over all 1,546 windows?
data: queues/manifest_scale.json: 1546 windows / 58 clips / 4.404 h, 1080p30 HEVC; label_source none
method: Per window: decode -> pixel26 at native fps, EG2 mean embedding, regime descriptors; frozen heads + equal-weight average; router; contract.jsonl with sha256 receipt
headline_result: n=1546/1546 scored, 0 decode failures, label_source none, descriptive. Verdicts: accept 296 (19.15%), reject 83 (5.37%), review 1167 (75.49%); profile factory_1080p30 1540 / default 6 (UNSEEN_REGIME); 0.683 windows/s, 5761 ms/window mean; 1546/1546 receipts re-verified.
why: Ship the contract file as the B2 PoC artefact; keep the frozen recipe. Do NOT read accept/reject shares as quality: no labels, and IndEgo-trained models did not transfer (0.4-0.53 AUROC, n_bad=9).

question: Can one deterministic command reproduce the documented baselines for PR comparison?
data: IndEgo gold n=150 (human); OOD ood_labels.json n=60 (51 good / 9 bad, human)
method: LOCO logistic + clip-bootstrap CI; frozen-model OOD with window-bootstrap CI; CPU sklearn, no network
headline_result: 26 per-pixel features LOCO C=0.3 -> AUROC 0.8100 (clip-bootstrap 95% CI 0.693-0.887); EG2 window embedding C=0.01 -> 0.8480 (0.734-0.909). OOD: frozen IndEgo pixel26 does NOT transfer, 0.4314 at fps=10.
why: Use eval/standard/run_all.py as the single comparison number for PR-triggered review.

question: Do the published baselines, E1.01-E1.02 fps sweeps and E3.01-E3.05 policy reproduce independently?
data: IndEgo human gold 150 windows / 7 clips (READ-ONLY); cached features; OOD labels 60 (9 bad)
method: Re-run pinned scripts from pod/base; E1.02 re-implemented from scratch; LOCO + clip-bootstrap 95% CI; exact-match tolerance at published precision
why: Cheapest defence against a silent protocol bug; adopted stack verified on the in-domain/CPU half. GPU feature-extraction and frozen-OOD runs remain UNVERIFIED (no CUDA here; labels2 absent).

question: Do the adopted every-2nd + 4 s + EG2-2fps + pixel settings integrate into one scorer path?
data: IndEgo human gold 150 windows / 7 clips (cached features, CPU); OOD 60 descriptive only
method: LOCO over 7 clips re-fitting both views at the 4 s prefix; equal-weight fusion; frozen verdict rule; every-2nd grid; clip-bootstrap CI
headline_result: Fused 4 s AUROC 0.874 [0.742,0.942], balanced acc 0.740; EG2 4 s 0.860; pixel26 4 s 0.797. Verdicts over 150 windows: accept 108 / reject 27 / uncertain 15; every-2nd samples 77/150 (51.3%); clip verdicts 5/7 model-based agree.
why: Integrates the adopted settings into jadal/poc_stream/policy.py and regenerates verdicts; OOD rows are descriptive-only (no OOD/accuracy claim). Loader now verifies the frozen sha256.

question: Are the explainer/deck/submission pack regenerated from FACTS + registry after the OOD failure?
data: FACTS.md snapshot + union registry (no new measurement)
method: Regenerate docs from FACTS.md + registry; fold in the LB1 verification note wherever 0.529 appears
headline_result: Explainer/deck/submission pack/POC_STATUS regenerated from FACTS + registry; the 0.529 PoC-cascade vs 0.415 frozen-ensemble distinction folded into every occurrence.
why: The old explainer/deck/pack predated the out-of-domain failure and the corrections; this is the current-consistent documentation set.

question: Is the frozen pre-registered OOD run staged as one reproducible command?
data: Frozen scorer bytes + 160 OOD windows; labels2 pending
method: Recover the byte-exact frozen config from git, anchor it with sha256, stage a one-command guarded run
headline_result: Byte-exact pre-registered config recovered and anchored (sha256 4da1068a...) at configs/frozen/ensemble_v1.prereg.json; guarded run staged. The OOD score itself is PENDING until labels2 land.
why: Closes the pre-registration gap found by LB1 (the shipped config was path-remapped, breaking the frozen hash); fail-closed one-command run for when labels arrive.

question: Which branches can merge and in what order?
data: 28 open PRs at the triage snapshot; git refs + live PR state
method: git merge-base / merge-tree / diff name-status per head; live gh PR inventory; full test-suite run on a clean main export
headline_result: 28 open PRs, 0 already ancestors of main, 19 merge-tree clean / 9 conflicting; main is green at test level (493 passed / 0 failed) modulo 4 pod-env collection errors (fastapi, imagehash); pod/base has 4 real failures from stale router fixtures.
why: Provides the merge-queue map and flags the duplicate-add hazard (experiments/registry.jsonl in 9 PRs) and the pod/base router-test defect for owners.

question: How far can resolution and CRF be cut before the 26-feature view degrades beyond 0.02 AUROC?
data: IndEgo gold 150 windows (100 good / 50 bad, human), re-encoded at a (resolution x CRF) grid; RES.04 OOD n=60 (51 good / 9 bad, human)
method: Re-encode each window with libx264 veryfast at res {480,360,240,180,120}p x CRF {18,23,28,33}; re-extract the 26 per-pixel features through the same frozen 160x90 path; identical LOCO logistic C=0.3 + clip-bootstrap CI (B=1000, seed 0). RES.04: frozen pixel-26 head on downscaled Ego10K (decode-time downscale, no re-encode). Cached 480p-native baseline 0.8100.
headline_result: RES.01 resolution: 240p 0.808, 180p 0.843, 120p 0.802 - all within 0.02 of 480p-native 0.8100, no knee down to 120p (180p = ~31% of bytes). RES.02 compression (480p): CRF28 0.7960 (delta -0.014) at 57% of CRF23 bytes; CRF33 0.7946 (delta -0.015) at 36%. RES.03 cross: 360p@CRF28 0.8036 at 257 KiB = best shipping point (~40% of the 480p@CRF23 bytes). RES.04 OOD-neutral: 480p delta -0.002, 360p delta +0.013 vs 1080p.
why: Resolution/CRF are bytes/transport levers, not feature levers: the frozen pipeline already decodes to 160x90, so dropping to 120p costs no AUROC and the win is bytes. Adopt 360p@CRF28 as the shipping point; CRF28/33 hold the <=0.02 budget and nothing regressed within the tested range. RES.04 (OOD) is neutral but its EG2 view was not recomputed, so EG2 resolution transfer is unverified. (RES.01-.03 adopt, RES.04 maybe.)

question: Can we drop sections ANYWHERE (middle/end/evenly), not just the start, and keep the clip verdict?
data: IndEgo gold 150 windows / 7 clips (human) + cached OOF probs
method: Per-clip 5-section subsampling: section-drop rules (1-2 of 5), stratified vs contiguous probes, dense-where-uncertain; clip bad-fraction error + clip-verdict agreement vs processed %; clip-bootstrap CI (B=2000).
headline_result: uniform-every-2 stays best (51.5% processed, bad-fraction error 0.049 [0.019,0.087], 7/7 verdict agreement). Dropping the START is worst (drop2-start err 0.189; drop1-start 0.110). Stratified 1/section 0.142; contiguous-probe 0.211. No section-skip policy is cheaper within tolerance.
why: Measured negative for 'skip sections anywhere'; it re-affirms E3. The START is the cleanest section (bad rate 0.09 sec1 -> 0.58 sec5), so dropping it is worst; END/EVENLY are the safest drops but are still dominated by every-2. Keep every-2nd (+4 s exit) as the only adopted sampler. (SKIP.01 maybe / SKIP.02 drop / SKIP.03 adopt re-affirms.)

question: Can lower-res/denser mosaic tiles be FASTER than sequential frames at the SAME accuracy, and does a denser low-res mosaic change the E2 verdict?
data: IndEgo gold 150 windows (100 good / 50 bad, human), 7 clips, all 480p source; LOCO over 7 clips
method: Build mosaics (EG2, logistic C=0.01, max_soft_tokens=140) at tile_px {224,160,112,96,64} and grids 2x2..6x6; clip-bootstrap CI B=1000, seed 0; matched mean-of-frames control; equal-canvas duel; timestamp/order ablations; wall-ms on a 48-window sample split into build vs EG2-embed.
headline_result: Tiles 112-160 px keep accuracy and get cheaper (-36% build+embed ms, -74% canvas); <96 px degrades (96 px 0.762, 64 px 0.736). Denser low-res grids DROP (2x2 0.722 ... 6x6 0.760, all below matched mean-of-frames). Equal-canvas duel: 4x4/168 px 0.845 vs 3x3/224 px 0.785 (+0.060 AUROC at -2.4 ms/win). Timestamps +0.021; tile order ~irrelevant. Best mosaic 0.845 still <= mean-of-frames N16 0.861 and only ties the EG2 baseline 0.848.
why: 'Same accuracy, faster' genuinely holds vs the 224 px mosaic, but at MATCHED frame count the mosaic still loses to mean-of-frames at every density, so the E2 verdict stands. Adoptable only as a cost optimisation for a mosaic-based pipeline and as an evidence artefact, not as a replacement for mean-of-frames. (MR.01 adopt / MR.03 maybe / MR.02 drop.)

question: Can the frozen E8.01 review share be cut below 60% with a symmetric abstain band on the raw score (no calibration)?
data: 1,546 unlabelled Ego10K windows (review denominator, label_source none) + 150 IndEgo gold (human, LOCO) + OOD-60 (51 good / 9 bad, evaluation only)
method: Sweep the symmetric abstain-band half-width w on the RAW frozen score; in-domain error = gold LOCO balanced accuracy over decided windows (clip-bootstrap CI B=2000); global temperature / Platt / isotonic fit LOCO on gold only, never on E8/OOD.
headline_result: Raw w=0.16 (band [0.34,0.66]) -> review 53.4% (from E8.01 75.5%) at gold BA 0.846 (err 0.154, 6/100 good rejected). Prescribed-grid crossings: <60% w=0.16 (53.36%); <50% w=0.14 (45.08%); <40% w=0.12 (37.00%). Calibration does not cut review at equal error; Platt/isotonic are harmful (LOCO BA 0.71 / 0.725 vs 0.795 raw).
why: Meets the <60% review-workload goal with NO model change. Calibration is a measured negative: a monotone map cannot reorder the error/review frontier, so it adds nothing at equal error. OOD decisions stay near chance (0.41-0.53 AUROC, n_bad=9), so this is a review-WORKLOAD result, not an accuracy claim.

question: Does decision-theoretic cost-margin gating cut the review share at equal accuracy?
data: 1,546 unlabelled Ego10K windows (descriptive) + 150 IndEgo gold (human, cached LOCO-OOF) + OOD-60 (51/9, evaluation only)
method: Selective classification: decide the top-`coverage` windows by cost-margin |p - p*| where p* = C_fa/(C_fa+C_fr); sweep coverage and cost ratio; in-domain = gold LOCO balanced accuracy over decided windows (clip-bootstrap CI); no decode.
headline_result: coverage 0.45, cost 1:1 -> review 55.0% (1,546) at gold BA 0.837 [0.645,0.937] (68 decided: 41 accept / 27 reject; on gold FP 4/100, FN 7/50). Asymmetric costs 2:1 / 5:1 are worse on gold (weighted err 0.309 / 0.382 vs 0.162 at 1:1) -> rejected. OOD BA 0.496 (eval only).
why: Cost-margin gating cuts review (frozen band 75.5% -> 55.0%) at gold BA 0.837, with no new inference and no new model; keep the symmetric 1:1 cost because asymmetric costs are a measured negative. OOD decisions remain ~chance, so it is a workload result, not an accuracy claim. (Pairs with Y2.02.)

question: Does a deterministic stage-0 quality-REJECT overlay on the review windows cut the review share further, safely?
data: 1,546 unlabelled Ego10K windows (descriptive); 150 IndEgo gold (human); synthetic degradation windows for rule derivation
method: Fixed a-priori stage-0 rules (TOO_DARK / OVEREXPOSED / FROZEN / NO_ACTIVE_WORK) over cached descriptor features; validated on 6-window-per-degradation synthetics and on the 150 gold windows; applied to the Y2.01 gating review set. No decode.
headline_result: Gating 55.0% -> 54.0% review; stage-0 fires on 2.5% (39/1,546; 15 inside the review set). On gold it fires 3/150 only (precision_bad 0.667, recall_bad 0.04). Adding gold-LOCO temperature is a no-op (54.0%).
why: A small, deterministic, decode-free overlay (-1.0 pt review) on top of cost-margin gating. The win is real but tiny and the gold n is 3, so it is not a certified quality-reject rule (the funnel found no safe quality rule on gold). Adopt as an overlay, not as an accuracy lever.

question: Which cached views exist, and does the frozen two-view baseline reproduce?
data: 150 IndEgo gold windows (human, nested LOCO); 60 OOD (eval only); cached features only
method: Nested LOCO per view (outer 7 clips; inner LOCO picks C); reproduce the frozen prob-average baseline; inventory available/absent cached views; report ambiguity mass at [0.4,0.6] and the profile band [0.25,0.75].
headline_result: Cached views: pixel26 (26), eg2 (768), perpixel121, physics16, theory18, series16. Baseline reproduces: prob-avg 0.8336 (matches nested_loco.json:ensemble_probavg), frozen fixed-C anchor 0.8534, per-view EG2 0.8458 / pixel26 0.7916 (match the frozen oof_probs.npz). EG2@1fps / @0.5fps absent (segments.npz is 2 fps only).
why: Reproduces the frozen two-view baseline exactly and inventories the cached views before any fusion claim; adopted as the reference the Y3 fusion sweep is measured against.

question: Does adding more cached views or switching prob-avg -> rank-avg cut the REVIEW share at equal or better AUROC?
data: 150 IndEgo gold windows (human, nested LOCO); 60 OOD (eval only); cached views only
method: Nested-LOCO combo sweep: pixel26/eg2 (+perpixel121, physics16, series16, theory18), probavg vs rankavg; report AUROC [clip-bootstrap CI] and ambiguity mass at [0.4,0.6] and the profile band [0.25,0.75].
headline_result: Rank-average of the existing two views is a free win: AUROC 0.8336 -> 0.8440, profile-band [0.25,0.75] review mass 0.653 -> 0.607. EG2-only cuts most (band 0.420, AUROC 0.846) but drops the pixel head. Adding perpixel121 / physics16 / series16 / theory18 is flat-to-worse (AUROC 0.807-0.843, band up to 0.807).
why: 'More cached views' is a CLEAN NEGATIVE: extra views do not raise AUROC and raise the ambiguity mass. The only adopted change is rank-average fusion of the two EXISTING views (free, no new inference); EG2-only is a maybe pending held-out confirmation. All AUROC differences are within the clip-bootstrap CI.
